newsitem.title: USA: Virginia to study sites for regional airport.
newsitem.headline: Virginia to study sites for regional airport.

text.p: Virginia Department of Aviation will conduct a study of airport needs in central and eastern Virgnia, identifying possibly sites for a major regional airport, state officials said.
A regional airport would cost at least $1 billion but probably would not be needed until 2030.

The $1.3 million study will start in December and take 18 months to two years to complete. It is the second phase of a two-part study that previously determined the existing airports in Richmond, Norfolk and Newport News can handle anticipated traffic growth through 2030.

Beyond that, the region will have to consolidate all three airports into one major new airport, or keep Richmond International in the west and build a new airport or expand one of the existing ones in the east, the first phase of the study found.

The second phase will determine which of those options the state should pursue, said state Transportation Secretary Robert Martinez. It will also examine the possiblity of building an industrial center next to a new airport to promote air cargo shipping.
